title: The Bug That Only Appeared on Fridays
sentences: Every Friday afternoon, our checkout page slowed to a crawl, and nobody on the team could explain why.
At first we blamed the network, then the database, and finally the unlucky intern who had merged the last change.
I decided to approach the problem methodically instead of chasing every rumor that drifted through the team chat.
After comparing the logs from several weeks, I noticed a pattern that was almost too subtle to see.
A scheduled report, written years ago by someone long gone, ran every Friday and quietly locked the main orders table.
Its behavior was so idiosyncratic that our monitoring tools had simply learned to ignore it.
The original author had left a cryptic comment promising to fix the query later, which of course never happened.
Rewriting that report felt daunting, but leaving it untouched was no longer a tenable option for the business.
We split the work into small, verifiable steps and wrote tests that reproduced the slowdown on demand.
When the fix shipped, the Friday complaints vanished, and my manager admitted the solution was surprisingly elegant.
Since then, I treat every mysterious bug as a puzzle rather than a nuisance, and I document my reasoning meticulously.

vocab.meaning: peculiar to one person or thing; unusual and individual
vocab.example: Her idiosyncratic naming style made the old code hard to follow.

vocab.meaning: able to be defended or maintained
vocab.example: Shipping without regression tests is not a tenable strategy.
The error message was so cryptic that we had to read the source code.

vocab.meaning: with great care and attention to every detail
vocab.example: She meticulously checked every edge case before signing off.
He worked through the checklist methodically, one item at a time.

vocab.meaning: seeming difficult and likely to discourage you
vocab.example: Migrating the whole test suite looked daunting at first.
The flaky test had become a real nuisance for the whole team.

focus.title: The two TH sounds: /θ/ and /ð/
focus.tip: Para /θ/ (through, methodically) pon la punta de la lengua entre los dientes y sopla aire sin voz, como la 'z' de España. Para /ð/ (the, then, that) haz lo mismo pero haciendo vibrar la voz; no la conviertas en una 'd' dura.

drills.prompt: The old report's behavior was so ____ that the monitoring tools ignored it.
drills.why: Idiosyncratic means peculiar to one thing, unlike anything else.

drills.prompt: Keeping the slow report was no longer a ____ option for the business.
drills.why: Tenable means it could still be defended or maintained.

drills.prompt: The author left a ____ comment that nobody could fully understand.
drills.why: Cryptic means mysterious and hard to understand.

drills.prompt: Rewriting a system you did not build can feel ____ at first.
drills.why: Daunting describes a task that looks hard enough to discourage you.

speak: Describe a problem at work or at home that you solved by being patient and methodical. What did you learn from it?
